key_insight: The paper explores whether alignment between sensory representations and motion trajectories can serve as a low-cost proxy for embodied policy success. The supplied abstract is incomplete, so it does not establish whether this relationship was validated.
problem_solved: Evaluating robotic foundation models typically requires costly closed-loop rollouts, creating a need for inexpensive offline indicators of policy capability.
method: Extend the Platonic Representation Hypothesis—which proposes convergence toward shared representations across modalities—to robot motion trajectories.
Investigate whether sensory representations become more aligned with motion representations as embodied models become more capable.
Explore sensorimotor alignment as an offline proxy for policy success; specific metrics and experimental results are not available in the supplied excerpt.
impact: If validated, sensorimotor alignment could help practitioners compare and screen robotic policies before running expensive robot evaluations. It would provide a capability signal, not necessarily replace closed-loop testing.

paper_title: Sensorimotor Alignment: A Platonic Proxy for Embodied Policy Success
